title: The ephemeral filesystem: what is lost when a container dies

videos.script: Every container has a writable layer, and this lesson is about how long it lasts. {{stop}} Stopping a container keeps it. Ana writes a note, stops the container, starts it, and the note is there. {{rm}} Removing it does not. Same name, same image, and the note is gone, because the name was never the container. {{db}} Then the expensive version. A database, a table, one row. Remove the container, run it again, and the table does not exist. {{volume}} Except the data was not deleted. It was sitting in a volume nobody named, and you will get it back. {{state}} The lesson ends with a rule. Treat every container as something you will delete, and put each kind of state somewhere that outlives it.
